query: Two Sets of Marks Your returned essay has two sets of marks. The marker's, in polite pencil: "Good." And another, in red ink and unsigned, in a small round hand, savaging every paragraph and fixing three of them. The last line reads: "You can do better than good. Paragraph four proves it." Rewrite it properly You rewrite it twice. On the third morning you leave it on the second-floor stair, where you found the first. By evening it's gone. Bin it Good is good. You drop the red pages in the scorched-room bin, and feel a little foolish about how much you want to fish them out.

Hm.
Thorne has handed {o}'s essay back for the third week running, more red ink than black. "Hm," he said, which is all he said. {o} is close to tears in the corridor. "He hates me. He doesn't do this to anyone else. Will you talk to him? He listens to you."
